In [[geodesy]], a '''map projection of the triaxial ellipsoid''' maps Earth or some other [[astronomical body]] modeled as a [[triaxial ellipsoid]] to the plane. Such a model is called the [[reference ellipsoid]]. In most cases, reference ellipsoids are [[spheroids]], and sometimes [[spheres]]. Massive objects have sufficient gravity to overcome their own rigidity and usually have an oblate ellipsoid shape. However, minor moons or [[Small Solar System body|small solar system bodies]] are not under [[hydrostatic equilibrium]]. Usually such bodies have irregular shapes. Furthermore, some of [[List of gravitationally rounded objects of the Solar System|gravitationally rounded objects]] may have a tri-axial ellipsoid shape due to rapid rotation (such as [[Haumea]]) or unidirectional strong tidal forces (such as [[Io (moon)|Io]]).

== Examples ==
A triaxial equivalent of the [[Mercator projection]] was developed by [[John P. Snyder]].<ref name="John P. Snyder">{{cite journal |last1=Snyder |first1=J. P. |title=Conformal Mapping of the Triaxial Ellipsoid |author-link1= John P. Snyder|year=1986 |journal= Survey Review |volume=28 |issue= 217 |pages=130–148 |doi=10.1179/sre.1985.28.217.130 }}</ref>

Equidistant map projections of a triaxial ellipsoid were developed by Paweł Pędzich.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pędzich |first1=Paweł |year=2017 |title= Equidistant map projections of a triaxial ellipsoid with the use of reduced coordinates |journal= Geodesy and Cartography |volume=66 |issue= 2 |pages=271–290 |doi=10.1515/geocart-2017-0021 |bibcode=2017GeCar..66..271P |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Conic Projections of a triaxial ellipsoid were developed by Maxim Nyrtsov.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nyrtsov  |first1=Maxim  |date=Winter 2017 |title= Conic Projections of the Triaxial Ellipsoid: The Projections for Regional Mapping of Celestial Bodies |journal= Cartographica: The International Journal for Geographic Information and Geovisualization |volume=52 |issue= 4 |pages=322–331 |doi=10.3138/cart.52.4.2017-0002 |url=https://www.proc-int-cartogr-assoc.net/1/84/2018/ }}</ref>

Equal-area cylindrical and azimuthal projections of the triaxial ellipsoid were developed by Maxim Nyrtsov.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nyrtsov  |first1=Maxim V. |year=2015 |title= Equal-Area Projections of the Triaxial Ellipsoid: First Time Derivation and Implementation of Cylindrical and Azimuthal Projections for Small Solar System Bodies |journal=The Cartographic Journal |volume=52 |issue= 2 |pages=114–124 |doi= 10.1080/00087041.2015.1119471 |s2cid=124797916 |url= https://www.researchgate.net/publication/285545182 |accessdate=9 February 2019}}</ref>

Jacobi conformal projections were described by [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Nyrtsov  |first1=Maxim V. |title=Cartography from Pole to Pole  |publisher=Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg |date=2014 |pages= 235–246 |chapter=Jacobi Conformal Projection of the Triaxial Ellipsoid: New Projection for Mapping of Small Celestial Bodies |isbn=978-3-642-32617-2}}</ref>
